reason: Selected sections support a raw-trace-access ablation and show retrieval-policy differences between models. The terminal benchmark was also used for search, so those scores are not untouched final evaluation.

candidates.title: Keep raw traces inspectable during harness search
candidates.rule: When a coding-agent proposer searches classification harnesses, let it inspect prior code, scores, and raw execution traces on demand; compare this with giving it scores or fixed summaries alone.
candidates.passage: Access to raw execution traces is the key ingredient for enabling harness search.
candidates.finding: In the classification interface ablation, full-trace access produced median accuracy 50.0 versus 34.6 for scores-only and 34.9 for scores plus summaries. The intervention is the proposer interface, not a claim that every raw trace should be injected into every task prompt.
workloads: Online text classification; USPTO, Symptom2Disease and LawBench
candidates.conditions: The proposer can selectively inspect a filesystem history of candidate code, scores and executions. The ablation is reported in classification; results from other domains do not isolate this component.
candidates.limitations: One paper and one strong proposer configuration. Raw traces may contain sensitive material and still need access controls. The separately reported TerminalBench-2 experiment searches and evaluates on the same tasks; it is not evidence of blind generalization.
candidates.validation_test: Hold the proposer, evaluation budget and classification tasks fixed. Compare scores-only, scores-plus-summaries and selectively accessible raw traces, then evaluate the selected harness on a separate task set.

candidates.title: Check retrieval-policy gains separately for each model
candidates.rule: When choosing a math-retrieval harness, compare candidate retrieval policies on each intended model instead of assuming the policy with the best cross-model average wins on every model.
candidates.passage: the regressions observed with dense retrieval and random few-shot prompting across several models.
candidates.finding: Table 6 reports both gains and regressions from fixed retrieval choices. The learned policy has the best average, but BM25 scores 46.6 versus its 46.3 for Gemini-3-Flash. The recommendation to select per deployment is inferred from those differences; that selection procedure is not itself tested.
workloads: 200 held-out IMO-level problems drawn from IMO-AnswerBench, IMO-ProofBench and ArXivMath
candidates.conditions: The corpus is decontaminated; one policy was selected using GPT-OSS-20B on a separate search set. Accuracy averages three samples per problem.
candidates.limitations: The 0.3-point single-model difference is not evidence of a statistically reliable winner. These results do not show that transfer always fails: the learned policy improves over no retrieval for all five models.
candidates.validation_test: Compare no retrieval, BM25 and the proposed policy at the same resource budget on representative tasks for each target model. Choose using development tasks and confirm with a final held-out test.

review_scope: Focused reading of abstract/introduction and selected main-text results, ablations and limitations; intervening sections, references and appendices were not comprehensively reviewed.
